title: What My Grandfather Taught Me About Asking Permission
script: Narrator: [warmly] My grandfather was a quiet man, but he noticed everything. He never scolded loudly, yet his lessons stayed with me for life.
Narrator: [thoughtful] When I was young, I once walked into his room and took his newspaper without asking. I thought it was a small thing.
Narrator: [gently] He did not shout. He simply asked, did you ask permission before taking that? I said no, and I felt suddenly small.
Narrator: [reflective] He explained that asking permission is not about the object itself. It is about respecting another person's space and belongings.
Narrator: [softly] From that day, I started asking before touching anything that was not clearly mine, even small things, even at home.
Narrator: [warmly] My grandfather also taught me to ask permission before entering someone's house, even close family, by knocking and greeting first.
Narrator: [thoughtful] He said this habit protects everyone's dignity, and it shows that you value the other person's comfort, not just your own convenience.
Narrator: [honestly] At first, I thought these rules were too formal, almost old-fashioned for modern life.
Narrator: [gently] But as I grew older, I noticed how rare this habit had become, and how much people appreciated it when I practiced it.
Narrator: [warmly] Friends started telling me I was thoughtful and easy to trust, simply because I asked before borrowing or entering.
Narrator: [reflective] Now I try to teach the same lesson to younger people around me, the same quiet lesson my grandfather taught me.
Narrator: [peacefully] He passed away a few years ago, but I still hear his calm voice whenever I reach for something that is not mine.
Narrator: [with feeling] A simple question, may I, carries more respect than people realize. My grandfather understood that better than anyone I have known.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do as a child that upset his grandfather slightly?
options: He took his grandfather's newspaper without asking
quiz.explanation: He walked into his grandfather's room and took the newspaper without asking permission.

quiz.question: According to the grandfather, what is asking permission really about?
options: Respecting another person's space and belongings
Following strict rules for no reason
quiz.explanation: The grandfather explained it is about respecting another person's space and belongings, not the object itself.

quiz.question: What else did the grandfather teach about entering houses?
options: Walk in without knocking to save time
Knock and greet first, even at close family's homes
quiz.explanation: He taught the narrator to knock and greet first before entering someone's house, even close family.

quiz.question: How did the narrator's habit affect his friends' view of him?
options: They found him thoughtful and easy to trust
quiz.explanation: Friends told him he was thoughtful and easy to trust because he asked before borrowing or entering.

quiz.question: What does the narrator do now with this lesson?
options: He tries to teach it to younger people around him
He keeps it only to himself
He no longer believes in it
quiz.explanation: He now tries to teach the same lesson to younger people around him.
